definitions.gloss: to refuse; to reject; to deny
definitions.explanation: To firmly and categorically refuse a request, demand, or proposal. Stronger and more definitive than simply declining.

examples.japanese: {要求|ようきゅう}を{拒絶|きょぜつ}した。
{彼女|かのじょ}は{面会|めんかい}を{拒絶|きょぜつ}した。
examples.english: She refused to meet with them.

examples.japanese: {移植|いしょく}された{臓器|ぞうき}を{体|からだ}が{拒絶|きょぜつ}する{場合|ばあい}がある。
examples.english: There are cases where the body rejects a transplanted organ.

notes:
A strong word for refusal that implies a firm, absolute rejection. Composed of {拒|きょ} (resist, refuse) + {絶|ぜつ} (sever, cut off). The double emphasis on cutting off makes this stronger than {断|ことわ}る or {拒否|きょひ}する.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {拒絶|きょぜつ}{反応|はんのう} — rejection reaction (medical, as in organ transplants)
- {要求|ようきゅう}を{拒絶|きょぜつ}する — to reject a demand
- {入国|にゅうこく}を{拒絶|きょぜつ}する — to refuse entry (to a country)
- {拒絶|きょぜつ}の{意思|いし}を{示|しめ}す — to indicate refusal

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {拒否|きょひ}する — to refuse, to deny; slightly less forceful, more common in everyday use
- {断|ことわ}る — to refuse, to decline; general-purpose, can be polite
- {却下|きゃっか}する — to reject (an application, proposal); official/administrative

REGISTER:
Formal and somewhat literary. More common in writing, news, and legal/medical contexts than in everyday conversation.
